_about: The ONE list of the MQTT topics of A.R.M.O.R.: who publishes each, who reads it, which schema its messages follow, the QoS it travels with and whether the broker keeps it. tools/generate_asyncapi.py writes asyncapi/armor-mqtt.asyncapi.json from it and tests/test_mqtt_topics.py compares it with the access lines of node_roles.json (a role may publish exactly the topics it is listed for, and read exactly the ones it is listed to read). Roles: the keys of node_roles.json, and `server` (ARMOR-SERVER, whose lines are in ARMOR-DEVOPS scripts/armor_server.acl). {node_id} is the name of the node (^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}$).

channels.about: What a radar node sees: the tracks and the light.
The presence of a radar or a wall panel (not the health report, which is armor/health/{node_id}).
Name, firmware and address of a radar node or a wall panel.
A command to a radar node. Never retained and sent at most once: an old command must never be delivered later.

lifecycle.about: The birth message of a node and its last will are sent on this topic at QoS 1 and kept by the broker, so a server that starts later learns that a node is gone.

channels.about: The health report of a node of any family.
The events of the perimeter engine of a radar node.
Reserved: the access list of a radar node allows reading it and no message is defined yet.
An inverter or a battery read by a solar gateway; the `kind` of the message says which.
A maintenance step on a battery (write capability); never retained.
The answer to a maintenance step.
The measurements and the switches of an electrical node.
A command to one switch; never retained.
The answer to a switch command.
What the panel of an alarm node is doing.
Arm, disarm or silence; never retained.
The answer to an alarm command.
What the server says about a Zigbee zone while it holds the radio; may be signed.
What the server asks of the panel (configuration hash, zone feed, signature).
An order to one node (restart, pause, standby, identify, diagnostics...); never retained.
An order to every node; an arm only, never an execute.
The answer to an order.
A node that is about to be quiet on purpose says so; kept by the broker so that a server that starts later also reads it.
What a network node sees of the local network.
The alert of the server for whoever listens (a siren, a screen).
The device layer: `{relay}/state`, `availability` and `set` of each device of a node. Free-form values, described by the device registry of the server.
